questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a position that lets you use your arms to control the motorcycle. Do not sit in a way that makes your arms hold up your body weight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: Refusing to take a breath test when an officer requests it:

options.text: Is your right and will have no negative consequences.

questions.explanation: By riding on Wisconsin roadways, you agree to take a chemical test if an officer requests it. Refusing a test will result in your license being suspended for at least one year.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a winding road ahead. Slow down to a safe speed for the curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a left turn. It is unsafe and against the law to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs are used in construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should NOT be used?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider's skill level.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan travel based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind experienced ones so they can be watched. Ride in a staggered formation for safety.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than you would without a passenger.
Brake later than you would without a passenger.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start slowing earlier, keep more distance from other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps before entering traffic.

questions.question: Increase your following distance if:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Increase your distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase your distance in heavy traffic or when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When being passed by another vehicle, be alert to:

options.text: Objects thrown from the other vehicle.
Wind gusts from the passing vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch out for the mirrors, body, and any objects from the passing vehicle. Be aware of wind gusts it creates. Also watch for objects thrown by passengers who may not be paying attention.

questions.question: When can you carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: Only if the passenger is a child.
Only if the passenger has a motorcycle license.
If your motorcycle is designed to carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: If your motorcycle is designed to carry a passenger.
questions.explanation: You can only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has the proper equipment for it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a stop sign is coming. Get ready to stop completely.

questions.question: Which helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has survived a previous crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance to more than four seconds?

options.text: When you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on wet roads, gravel roads, and when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead. You need extra space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire is flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear.
The back end jerks from side to side.
The rear brake does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually won't hear the tire fail.

questions.question: What should a good face shield NOT be?

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.explanation: A face shield should NOT be airtight. It needs to allow air to pass through to prevent fogging and keep you able to see clearly.

questions.question: What should you adjust when carrying a heavy load?
questions.explanation: Adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, and shocks to match the weight you are carrying.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and use both brakes if you need to stop. Avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. What should you wear?

options.text: You do not need brightly-colored clothing during the day.
You should wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
You should wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing when riding, even during the day. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible.
questions.explanation: Move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers at a blind intersection.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless another car is ahead or coming toward you), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing to be more visible. Always change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: It is important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is tailgating you. This warns the driver that you are about to slow down. It also helps if you are slowing down in a place where drivers do not expect it.

questions.question: When riding at night, a motorcyclist should:
questions.explanation: Night riding is dangerous because you cannot see as far and other drivers cannot see you as well. To stay safe, you should slow down, use your headlight fully, and keep a larger distance from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, you should:

options.text: Not worry about them and just focus on the road in front of you.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up makes it worse. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers do not expect you there and may leave the road suddenly.

questions.question: Where should you open up your following distance to more than four seconds?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. This includes slippery roads, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. If something is wrong, you must find it before riding in traffic or at high speeds.

questions.question: You should do all of the following to reduce your chances of a crash, except:

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Communicate your intentions by using your turn signals and brake light.
Search for hazards in your path.
Hope the other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope the other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers, tell them what you plan to do, and keep space around you. Look for hazards, identify them, and be ready to react.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. Instead, you will notice a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always be visible and tell other drivers what you plan to do. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: A "wobble," or sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars, can usually be caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
Improperly tightening the front wheel to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. Most wobbles come from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.
